info.title: Butler client API
info.description: The public subset of the Butler API that games and SDKs call. Generated from the Butler server spec by scripts/sync-spec.mjs; do not edit by hand.

post.description: Append-only event log written by game servers. Authenticated via game-server JWT; the integration is taken from the JWT claims, never from the body. user_id is a free-form game-side player identifier.

parameters.name: X-Butler-Signature
parameters.description: Required when calling Butler directly. `t` is Unix seconds; `v1` is hex HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<exact body bytes>` keyed with the integration signing secret. Valid for 300 seconds, each signature once. Doorman adds it for clients.

post.summary: Ingest a batch of game analytics events
post.description: Batch form of POST /v1/analytics/events for game servers. Takes up to 100 events, each validated with the single-event rules, and writes the valid ones in one insert. The response lists accepted/rejected per index; a rejected event never fails the batch. Same game-server JWT and X-Butler-Signature (over the whole body) as single ingest.

events.description: Up to 100 events, each shaped like the single-event body: { user_id, event_name, metadata?, timestamp?, tags?, event_id?, session_id? }.

get.summary: Fetch the remote analytics config for a build
get.description: Kill switch, per-event sample rates and batch cap for the calling integration, taken from the game-server JWT. `build` selects a per-build override when one exists. Sends an ETag and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=<ttl_s>`; a matching `If-None-Match` gets 304.

sample_rates.description: Event name (lowercase) to keep-probability, 0 to 1. Missing = 1.

get.summary: Start an OAuth authorization (code + PKCE S256)
get.description: Public. `response_type=code`, `client_id`, `redirect_uri` (exact match; native loopback may vary the port), `scope` (space separated, within the client's allowed scopes), `state` (required), `code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method=S256` (the only method). An unknown or disabled client, or an unregistered redirect URI, answers 400 JSON and never redirects. Other errors redirect to the client with `error`, `state` and `iss`. A valid request is stored for 10 minutes, a browser binding cookie is set, and the browser is redirected to the consent page with the request id only. When the browser is signed in, the request belongs to that account; another account signing in later in the same browser is refused.

post.summary: Exchange an authorization code, or rotate a refresh token
post.description: `grant_type=authorization_code` with `code`, `code_verifier` (S256), `client_id` and `redirect_uri`, all matching what the code was issued for; the code is single use, and a second use revokes the refresh family issued from it. `grant_type=refresh_token` with `refresh_token` and `client_id` (and optionally a narrower `scope`): rotates the family and re-intersects its scopes with the current effective scope; a refresh never gains scopes. Responses carry a game-player access token. Public clients, no secret. Errors are RFC 6749 §5.2 JSON.

get.summary: The signed-in player, as this game sees them (game-player token, profile:read)
get.description: Game-player token only (from POST /v1/oauth/token), for this integration, holding `profile:read` in both the token and the current effective scope. Returns the pseudonymous id, display name and avatar. Never a Butler id.

post.description: Exchange a game server's `client_id` + `client_secret` for a short-lived HS256 JWT (60 min TTL). Credentials are created in Backstairs. The issued JWT carries org_id, integration_id, tier, permissions, api_version, iat, and exp. Invalid credentials return a generic 401 to prevent client_id enumeration. Inactive integration or inactive owning org returns 403.

post.summary: Award an accolade to a player (game server, accolades:write)
post.description: Game server credential for this integration. `player_id` is the player's pseudonym for this game; an unknown pseudonym, an unlinked player and a revoked grant all answer 403 `PLAYER_NOT_LINKED`. Needs a consent grant holding the scope, within the integration ceiling; otherwise 403 `SCOPE_NOT_GRANTED`. Always the caller's own grant, never a sibling game's. For non-internal studios, an accolade that pays currency or that the studio owns (not this game) is refused with 403 `SCOPE_NOT_GRANTED`.
